sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: For Sare (Kapriman): stress non-contrastive and predictable from syllable count; secondary stress always on the first syllable; primary stress on the final syllable of disyllables and on the penultimate syllable of words of three or more syllables; affixed/compounded forms keep stress on the root. Also notes intonational pitch on particles (e.g. mba 'no' 'with a sustained levelled pitch'). Nothing about Bisis prosody.

sources.note: Footnote pp. 513-514 gives stress for other Sepik Hill languages only: 'Lewis and Lewis (1970) indicate that stress occurs on the first syllable of the word in Sanio-Hiowe. Stress typically occurs on the penultima in Sumariup and Alamblak.. Dye and Dye (1969) give evidence for phonemic tone-stress in Bahinemo.' Bisis appears only in cognate-percentage discussion (p. 483) and three phonetic forms in Table 137 ([tuʔu-s] 'head', [ʔato] 'path', [f'oʔo] 'pig'); no statement about Bisis stress.
